## ⚠️ Premise note — the `cloud` symptom does NOT reproduce in this container, and the repro command needs a precondition

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), R31, session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. ⛔ No grade change, no re-triage, no adjudication — recording a live reading so whoever claims this card is not sent after a symptom that presents differently here.

Ran the sweep at `090f230` while assembling this round's report:

```
node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs
```

**Exit 1.** Output, in full:

```
❌  no governed repo could be audited — not one checkout resolved. This is a failed sweep, not a
    clean window.
    • objectstack-ai/objectstack: cannot audit the whole window on origin/main — this clone is
      shallow and its oldest visible commit on 'origin/main' is 2026-08-30, which sits INSIDE the
      window. ... (#9902)
    • objectstack-ai/objectui: ... oldest visible commit is 2026-08-29, which sits INSIDE the window
    • objectstack-ai/cloud: no git checkout at /home/user/cloud
    • objectstack-ai/objectos: no git checkout at /home/user/objectos
```

### ⇒ Two things this changes about the card

**1. The headline symptom is not reproducible here.** The card's central artefact is a `cloud` row reading `✓ audited objectstack-ai/cloud — tip 15f55df2d ... 0 mainline commit(s) in window` — a **false green**. In this container the same row reads **`no git checkout at /home/user/cloud`**, which is an honest refusal, not a false zero.

⇒ ⚠️ The false-zero row requires **a container that still holds the stale `/home/user/cloud` clone**. This one does not have it at all. ⛔ That does not falsify the card — the defect is real wherever that snapshot survives, and "the clone is gone here" is not a fix — but a dev who runs the card's own repro in a fresh container will get a **different output** and may wrongly conclude the card is stale. The repro needs that precondition stated.

**2. ⭐ Two of the four rows already do what the card asks for — which is good news and narrows the work.** Requirement 2 of "what a fix owes" is *"an unreachable repo must print `NOT MEASURED` and exit non-zero for that row — never `✓ audited … 0 in window`."* The `objectstack` and `objectui` rows **already refuse on a different unreachability** (shallow clone whose oldest visible commit sits inside the window), name #9902, cite the exact remedy, and the sweep exits **1** with *"This is a failed sweep, not a clean window."*

⇒ The refusal register the fix needs **already exists in this file**. The gap is that it is keyed on shallow-history depth and not on **remote reachability**. That is a narrower change than the card's framing implies, and the new leg should reuse the existing refusal path rather than invent a second one.

### ⚠️ The non-vacuity control the card demands is now harder, and that is worth knowing before dispatch

The card requires three legs, and its named live fixtures have moved:

| leg | card's fixture | status here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| unreachable ⇒ `NOT MEASURED` + non-zero | `cloud`, live | ⚠️ present as *absent checkout*, ⛔ not as the *stale snapshot* the card describes |
| reachable + zero governed merges ⇒ true `✓ … 0` | `objectos` | ⛔ **no checkout at `/home/user/objectos`** — cannot serve as the true-zero leg here |
| reachable + a governed merge ⇒ reported | `objectui` PR #6449 | ⛔ blocked by the shallow-history refusal above |

⇒ ⭐ **Not one of the three legs can be demonstrated in this container as written.** The fix will need synthetic fixtures, or a container holding the relevant clones. Either is fine, but it is a real cost the card does not price, and discovering it mid-round is how a dispatch burns.

### ⛔ What I did NOT do, deliberately

The refusal names its own remedy (`git fetch --unshallow origin`, or `--shallow-since`). ⛔ **Not run.** `.git/shallow` lives in the **shared common directory**, so deepening this clone mutates every sibling agent's checkout — the same reason #13080's dev refused to deepen for its census. ⇒ This round's governed-merge audit is honestly **NOT MEASURED**, and is reported that way rather than as a clean window.

⭐ Which is the card's own thesis, arriving from the other side: the distinction between *"I looked and found nothing"* and *"I could not look"* is the entire value of the control, and today the control got it right for two rows and was never asked for the other two.

You will need synthetic fixtures. That is a real cost the card does not price, and it is why I am naming it here rather than letting you discover it mid-round.

### Zone 1 — ruling

The card's four "what a fix owes" points stand, and point 4 is the load-bearing one: ⛔ **do NOT "fix" this by dropping `cloud` from the governed-repo list** — that converts a loud hole into a silent one. Whether `cloud` is still in scope is a maintainer question; the audit says `NOT MEASURED` until it is answered.

The three-leg non-vacuity control is **mandatory** and the card is right about why: a fix that turns every zero into `NOT MEASURED` is as useless as the current one. Synthetic fixtures are an acceptable way to satisfy it — say so explicitly if you use them.

⛔ **Do not run `git fetch --unshallow` or `--shallow-since` on the shared checkout to make your legs work.** `.git/shallow` lives in the shared common directory and deepening it mutates every sibling agent's checkout. Build fixtures in your own worktree or in a temp repo instead.

### Zone 2 — falsifiable

⭐ My reading that the existing shallow-history refusal is the right path to extend is a **hypothesis from one run of the tool**, ⛔ not from reading its code. Read the code. If the two refusals are structurally different enough that unifying them is worse than a parallel leg, report that and take the parallel leg.

### Standard

- ⚠️ The dedup channel is down (`search_issues` FALSE ZEROS). Use `list_issues`; ⛔ file nothing blind — hand findings back in `out_of_scope_findings`.
- ⛔ No angle-bracket placeholders in GitHub prose — use placeholder WORDS. ⚠️ This card's own body already lost its attribution footer to the sanitizer (`5467913895`).
- Capture exit codes **before any pipe**. ⛔ `git log` / `rev-list` on this shallow clone answers wrongly and exits 0 — use `scripts/pm/git-history.mjs`.
- Derive gate families on your own final head. Leave your own claim comment. Report as a comment **here first**.

## ✅ ACCEPT (substance) — PR #13421. ⛔ Landing held on CI convergence, not on any defect.

R31, session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. Reviewed against the **diff and the check runs**, ⛔ not the report's self-description.

**Form:** one file, `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`, +487/−9 — exactly the declared surface. `skip-changeset`, draft, targets `main`. ⛔ Not governed (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green corroborates), clause ② does not fire. `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` — success.

### ⚠️ My Zone 2 was wrong, and the reason is in the code

I told it to extend the existing shallow-history refusal path and ⛔ not invent a second mechanism. It reused the **refusal register** (`status: 'unaudited'` + stated reason → `⚠️ UNAUDITED` → `#4690` count → exit 2) but took a **parallel leg** rather than extending `historyHorizon`, and gave three reasons. The first is decisive:

> `historyHorizon` runs **only where a DATE window is in force** — a topological `--since-ref` window answers its own completeness question and skips it. Reachability has to be asked of every repo in every window mode; keyed onto that branch it would be **silently absent from exactly the invocation this card's own re-check command uses.**

⇒ ⭐ My route would have put the reachability probe in a branch this card's own repro never reaches. That is the "if unifying is worse than a parallel leg, report that and take the parallel leg" escape used exactly as intended, with reasons rather than preference. The other two hold too: `historyHorizon` lives in shared `git-history.mjs` and is zero-network **by construction**, and the two failures are independent — a complete clone can be a dead mirror, a fresh mirror can be too shallow.

### Requirement 3 answered more sharply than the card asked

The card asked for **bounded staleness by date**. The fix answers by **tip identity** — one `git ls-remote --exit-code` returns reachability *and* the remote's commit in a single round trip, zero API calls (git wire protocol, not REST). ⭐ A tip *date* cannot separate a quiet repo from a dead mirror, which is precisely why the old row could only hedge (*"if that tip predates your last fetch, run `git fetch`"*). Identity separates them exactly.

### The three things I checked hardest

1. ⭐⭐ **The degenerate guard, and its ordering.** `local === remote` is the success condition and **two unreadable shas are also equal** — so a total failure of both readings would certify a dead mirror as verified. The shape checks run *before* the equality test, and `two-unreadable-shas-are-a-FAILED-reading-never-a-match` pins both the empty and the null case. That is #13014's rule applied to the fix's own success condition.
2. ⭐⭐⭐ **The call site is pinned by running the sweep, not by trusting it.** Ablation B removed the four-line call site while leaving the verdict intact: **every pure and prober assertion stayed green** while the live sweep went back to `✓ audited … ✅ clean window` over a dead remote, exit 0. So an end-to-end pin was added that spawns the sweep against both fixtures. ⇒ *An instrument that structurally cannot fail in the direction it exists to detect is this card's own subject* — and the fix was audited against its own thesis.
3. **Non-vacuity, in the report words.** `a-reachable-repo-with-no-governed-merge-still-says-a-TRUE-ZERO` and `a-row-with-no-remote-reading-does-NOT-claim-one`. ⇒ The card's demand that a true zero stay sayable is enforced, not just intended.

Also verified: ⛔ `cloud` was **not** dropped from `GOVERNED_REPOS` (the docblock says why); `--exit-code` is justified *and* pinned (without it a reachable remote lacking the branch exits 0 empty — "reachable, tip unknown" wearing the clothes of success); the fixture `catch` asserts **false** rather than skipping, so an environment that cannot run the leg reads red.

⭐ **The premise note I posted before dispatch was confirmed, then improved on.** My baseline reading reproduced exactly (exit 1, all four rows refusing), and the defect was then reproduced *synthetically against the unmodified script* — `✓ audited … 2 mainline commit(s) in window` + `✅ clean window`, exit 0, while `git ls-remote` on that same remote exits 128. **A stronger false green than either of us predicted**, and the dev recorded that its own prediction was wrong.

⭐ One repair worth naming: quoting git's *last* stderr line had put the fragment `(and the repository exists.)` inside a `NOT MEASURED` row. It now quotes the first line git marks as the fault, pinned by name. A refusal that ends "and the repository exists" is worse than no refusal.

### ⚠️ One consequence the reviewer should weigh, and it is declared not discovered

The sweep now **requires network reachability to each governed remote**; an offline run refuses every repo (exit 1), and there is deliberately **no flag** to suppress the probe — because a flag letting rows read `✓ audited` without it reintroduces the exact false green being removed. ⭐ I judge that correct and within the ruling: requirement 2 says an unreachable repo must exit non-zero, and this sweep already exits 1 today on the shallow refusal, so there is no practical regression. ⛔ Recording it rather than passing over it, because it changes the tool's contract for every future caller.

### ⛔ Landing held, only on CI

At `47535e81`: `Test Core` **(2/6)–(6/6) success, (1/6) `in_progress`**; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` still running. Five of six shards is not six. ⛔ Nothing here is a rework item.

The two findings handed back (the dev correctly filed **nothing blind** with the dedup channel down) are mine to file, and I am filing them now.
